newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: "Stals says S.Africa asset swaps some 15 bln rand".
newsitem.headline: "Stals says S.Africa asset swaps some 15 bln rand".

text.p: South African Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said on Thursday an estimated 15 billion rand in asset swaps had already taken place between South African and foreign institutions, Business Day said on Friday.

Asset swaps were introduced in July 1995 to allow South African investors, who operate under exchange control laws, to obtain foreign assets without materially affecting the level of the country's foreign exchange reserves, the newspaper said.
Stals told the paper South African companies' interest in foreign direct investment was beginning to wane as it seemed most of the big offshore moves had been completed.
He said most of the transactions currently being evaluated by exchange control officials were projects in Africa, which did not involve large amounts of money.

Stals did not want to be drawn on the timing of a further easing of foreign exchange controls but said it did not necessarily depend on very large increases in the foreign exchange reserves, Business Day said.
He agreed that reserves were still under pressure and said although he did not expect an improvement in the next two or three months there should be an increase in the second half of the year.
The paper said Stals believed "the corner had been turned" and that he felt reassured that South Africa would not need assistance from the International Monetary Fund in the current business cycle.

Earlier this week, Stals told Reuters he saw scope for a "very stable" rand in 1997, with the currency depreciating less than the inflation differentials between South Africa and its major trading partners. He put the differential at between seven and eight percent.

He forecast the current account of the balance of payments at about half of 1996's deficit which he estimated at around 10 billion rand. Consumer inflation should average less than 10 percent, he said.
